diagnosis.root_cause: The health-check alarm incorrectly reports all eight PONs as failed. The OLT, subscriber ONU, and sampled ONUs are reachable, online, authenticated, and have normal optical readings; OLT CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are also healthy.
evidence: The triggered condition claims all 8 PONs failed, but the OLT responds to ping and SNMP and its OID subtree responds.
The OLT metrics are normal: CPU 24%, memory 18%, temperature 42C, with a stable 58-day uptime.
The affected ONU is online, authenticated, completes the EPON exchange, and responds to live SNMP probing.
The affected ONU has strong/normal optical levels: RX about -19.7 dBm and TX about +2.4 dBm.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX variation is within approximately 0.3 dBm, TX variation is narrow, distance remains constant at 124, and TX bias remains healthy around 11 mA.
All sampled ONUs on EPON0/5 are online and responding, ruling out a PON-port or splitter outage for the subscriber's port.
The OLT has 207 of 214 ONUs online; seven offline is below the normal background level for this population and does not indicate an OLT-wide outage.
VLAN 1035 is present and matches the expected customer VLAN.
Authentication and sessions are normal: two sessions in 24 hours, seven-day activity within the normal baseline, long session durations, and no RADIUS mismatch.
The router heartbeat is healthy and router resource metrics are normal, so the alarm is not caused by router unreachability.
The evidence therefore indicates an erroneous OLT health-check result rather than a physical, optical, authentication, VLAN, router, or capacity fault.

remediation.action: Clear the false critical alarm after confirming the live probe results. Investigate and repair the PON health-check logic, data source, or result freshness that generated the 8/8 failure. Re-run the check against all eight PONs, verify alarm-to-service correlation, and add suppression or validation so a PON failure is not declared without corroborating ONU or interface loss.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
The record is internally consistent and only its date betrays it
Nothing in the alarm payload signals that it is stale
